prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. STYLE TAKES PRIORITY: STRICT 8-to-16-bit tabletop token pixel style. Replace all human bodies with SIX FLAT WOODEN COUNTERS bearing ONE LARGE ENGRAVED EQUIPMENT SYMBOL each. Absolutely NO anatomical characters, heads, faces, legs, clothes or normal RPG sprites. Allied counters round with pale teal rim and shield/bow/two-dagger carvings; hostile counters notched with oxblood rim and club/spear/bow carvings. Dark ink carvings, flat ochre wood, parchment board, six colors. Keep each engraved symbol at coarse 12x12-pixel scale; no wood grain, ornament or small lines. Two simple block obstacles, spike comb, irregular acid symbol. Sharply stair-stepped pixel edges, not smooth vector drawing. Create ONE complete readable tactical fantasy battlefield image, not a sprite sheet or collage. Common comparison scene: an isolated square 8-by-8 board (64 visible cells), shallow isometric view with broad 4:3 diamond tile tops, all edges visible, no perspective vanishing. Three small allied mercenaries occupy the near-left third: shield fighter, longbow archer, dual-dagger rogue. Three hostile fighters occupy the far-right third: broad club wielder, narrow spear wielder, jagged bow wielder. Each figure stands inside ONE cell; weapons and gaps separate silhouettes. Two solid stone blocks interrupt the middle; leave a clear route around them. A single raised floor-spike tile and a separate acid-puddle tile must differ by SHAPE, not only color. One ally has a double-corner selected-cell marker; three empty cells have tiny path dots; one short three-segment health bar is partly empty. Team identity uses round allied bases versus notched hostile bases as well as color. Keep floor calm, characters and hazards highest contrast. No extra actors, mage, scenery, text, numbers, logo, HUD panel, blur, bloom or random pixel noise. 4:3 landscape. Use crisp coarse square pixels throughout.
